regions.name: Dachigam
features: Dachigam National Park is located about 22 km from Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir

It is about 141 square kilometres and though it was a protected site, it was declared a national park in 1981. The word Dachigam means ‘ten villages’, referring to the villages relocated to create the park.
It is famous for the Hangul (Kashmir Stag), which is an endangered species found only here.
Dachigam has a rich biodiversity, which includes the Himalayan black bear, leopard, musk deer, and numerous bird species.

regions.name: Hemis
features: Located in Ladakh(Jammu and Kashmir), the Hemis National Park is famous for snow leopards.
It is the only national park in India which is located in the northern regions of the Himalayas.
It has the distinction of being the largest national park in India.

regions.name: Guindy
features: Guindy National Park is one of the smallest national parks, spanning an area of just 2.70 sq km.
It is located in Chennai in Tamil Nadu.
It is a green oasis in the heart of Chennai.

regions.name: Corbett
features: Jim Corbett National Park is located in the Nainital district in Uttarakhand and is considered to be the first national park established in 1936.
It is named after Jim Corbett, who played a main role in its creation.
It was the first park which was included by the government under Project Tiger in 1973.
The national park is home to the Bengal tiger, leopard, elephant, gharial, wild boar, and over 600 bird species.

regions.name: Kaziranga
features: Kaziranga National Park in Assam was established as a reserve forest in 1905 and declared a national park in 1974.
It was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1985.
It has about two-thirds of the world’s population of the one-horned rhinoceros.
It has also been declared as a Tiger Reserve in 2006.
Kaziranga has tigers, elephants, swamp deer, wild water buffalo, and hundreds of bird species, too.

regions.name: Nam Dhapa
features: Nam Dapha National Park lies in the international border between India and Myanmar (Burma) within Changlang District in the state of Arunachal Pradesh in northeast India.
It covers an area of 1985.23 square kilometres and is considered one of the largest protected areas in India.
It is famous for being the only national park in India which hosts four big cats. They are the tiger, the leopard, the snow leopard and the clouded leopard.
It was declared a national park in 1983 and also a Tiger Reserve.

regions.name: Gir
features: Gir National Park was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1965 and a national park in 1975.
It is located in the state of Gujarat and is the last refuge of the Asiatic lion.
It is roughly about 1412 square kilometres.
Gir is the only natural habitat in the world for Asiatic lions.

regions.name: Sanjay Gandhi
features: Sanjay Gandhi National Park is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
It is around 87 square kilometres and was established in 1996. It was earlier known as Borivali National Park.
The Kanheri Caves, which are a 2400-year-old Buddhist cave complex, are located in the national park.
The national park boasts a rich biodiversity with leopards, spotted deer, macaques, and over 250 bird species.

regions.name: Periyar
features: Periyar National Park is situated in the state of Kerala, and its core zone is about 350 square kilometres.
Periyar National Park was declared a sanctuary in 1934, and then it was declared a National Park in the year 1982.
It was declared a Tiger Reserve in 1978 under the Project Tiger.
It is famous for its large population of elephants.

regions.name: Rajaji
features: Rajaji Tiger Reserve spreads across Haridwar and Dehradun in the state of Uttarakhand.
This National Park boasts of more than 50 species of mammals including the highly  endangered Asian Elephant and Tiger.

regions.name: Nanda Devi
features: The Nanda Devi National Park is located in the upper reaches of the Himalayas in the state of Uttarakhand.
It is a part of the UNESCO World Heritage List
The snow leopard, the Himalayan musk deer and a diverse variety of plants are found in this national park.

regions.name: Dudhwa
features: The Dudhwa national park is situated in the state of Uttar Pradesh and is home to a diverse range of wildlife.
It is also known for its unique ecosystem with grasslands, swamps and dense forests.

regions.name: Sariska
features: Sariska Tiger Reserve is a national park situated in Alwar in the state of Rajasthan.
The national park spans over 800 square kilometres and is home to many animals apart from tigers.

regions.name: Desert Sanctuary
features: The Desert National Park spans about 3000 square kilometres  between Jaisalmer and Barmer districts of Rajasthan.
The national park features rolling sand dunes, jagged rocks and salt lakes.
The camel, black buck, chinkara and desert fox are all a part of the fauna of the national park.

regions.name: Vansada
features: Vansada national park is situated in the state of Gujarat.
It spans over an area of 24 square kilometres and has a variety of animals such as leopards, hyenas, bison, sambar deer, and four-horned antelopes, among others.
The national park is home to about 450 species of plants and over 200 species of birds.

regions.name: Silent Valley
features: Silent Valley National Park is located in the state of Kerala.
It was declared a National Park in 1984 and formally inaugurated in 1985.
41 mammals, 211 birds, 49 reptiles, 47 amphibians, 12 fishes, 164 butterflies and 400 species of moths are found here.

regions.name: Bandipur
features: Bandipur National Park is located in the southern part of Karnataka.
It has the second highest population of tigers in India.
It has a rich diversity of flora and fauna. Tigers, Indian Elephants, Leopard, Dhole, Sambar, Sloth bear, Chital are a few of the animals found here.

regions.name: Nagarhole
features: Nagarahole Tiger Reserve was previously known as Rajiv Gandhi (Nagarahole) National Park.
It is named after the river Nagarahole  which literally means ‘Serpent River’.
It is spread over Mysore and Kodagu and covers an area of 843.96 square kilometres.
It is acclaimed as a high-density tiger population area.

regions.name: Bannerghatta
features: The Bannerghatta National Park is located in the state of Karnataka.
It spans an area of 260.51 square kilometres and has a lion and tiger safari.

regions.name: Ranthambore
features: Ranthambore National park is one of the biggest national parks in northern India.
It is situated in the state of Rajasthan.
The national park has 40 species of mammals such as the  royal Bengal tiger, leopards, sloth bears, several species of deer etc

regions.name: Madhav
features: The Madhav Tiger Reserve is situated in the northern parts of Madhya Pradesh.
This national park has a lake, meadow and forest ecosystems.
It spans an area of almost 355 square kilometres.

regions.name: Panna
features: Panna Tiger Reserve is a tiger habitat located in Madhya Pradesh.
There are more than 200 species of birds other than wild animals such as leopards, wild dogs, hyaenas, sloth bears etc.

regions.name: Sanjay
features: The Sanjay Tiger Reserve is located in the Sidhi district of Madhya Pradesh.
It has a rich diversity of flora and fauna with many critically endangered species.

regions.name: Palamau
features: The Palamau Tiger Reserve is located in the state of Jharkhand.
It was established when Project Tiger was introduced in 1973.
The Tiger Reserve has mainly of Sal forests, mixed deciduous forests and bamboo groves.

regions.name: Similipal
features: Similipal National Park is located in the state of Odisha.
The Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
It is home to many endangered species such as the Royal Bengal tiger and the Indian Elephant

regions.name: Kanha
features: The Kanha Tiger Reserve is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
The state animal of Madhya Pradesh - Hard Ground Barasingha is exclusively found here. It is a species of deer.
The forests of Kanha has Sal and other mixed forest trees.

regions.name: Pench
features: The Pench National Park was established in 1975 and got the status of a Tiger Reserve in 1999.
It is located in the state of Maharashtra and has its name from the Pench River.
It is spread over 742 square kilometres.

regions.name: Nawegaon
features: The Nawegaon National Park is situated in the state of Maharashtra.
There are low hills surrounded by forests and this is considered a key biodiversity area.

regions.name: Indravati
features: Indravati National Park is located in the state of Chhattisgarh and gets its name from the nearby Indravati River.
It is home to rare wild buffaloes and is a Tiger Reserve from 1983.

regions.name: Indravati
features: Indravati National Park is located in the state of Chhattisgarh and gets its name from the nearby Indravati River.
It is home to rare wild buffaloes and is a Tiger Reserve from 1983.

regions.name: Kinnerasani
features: Kinnerasani is located in the state of Telangana.
It is named after the river Kinnerasani which flows through it.
Panthers, tigers and wild boar abound here.

regions.name: Kinnerasani
features: Kinnerasani is located in the state of Telangana.
It is named after the river Kinnerasani which flows through it.
Panthers, tigers and wild boar abound here.

regions.name: Kanger Valley
features: The Kanger Valley National Park is located in the state of Chhattisgarh.
It encompasses an area of 200 square kilometres and has remarkable geological formations.
It has 49 species of mammals and 201 species of avian population.

regions.name: Papikonda
features: Papikonda National Park is located in the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
It covers an area of 1068 square kilometres and is situated along the banks of the Godavari River.
There are dense forests and grasslands with abundant wildlife.

regions.name: Coringa
features: Coringa Sanctuary is situated in the state of Andhra Pradesh.
It is named after a tiny village  Coringa situated in  the east Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh.
It has 24 species of mangroves and numerous species of wildlife.

regions.name: Sundarbans
features: The Sundarbans National Park covers 10,000 square kilometres of land and water. More than half of it is in India and the rest in Bangladesh.
It has the world’s largest area of mangrove forests and single largest population of tigers.

regions.name: Parmadan
features: Parmadan is officially known as Bibhutibhushan Wildlife Sanctuary.
It is located in the state of West Bengal.
It is situated on the banks of the Ichamati River.

regions.name: Bethuadhar
features: Bethuadahari Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of West Bengal.
It has about 50 species of birds and is home to diverse fauna such as Chital, Jungle cat, Civet cat, Jackal, Mongoose, Porcupine, Langur, Monitor lizard, Python, Cobra, Krait etc.

regions.name: Nokrek
features: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve  is located in the state of Meghalaya.
It has evergreen forests covering 90% of its area.
It is home to unique and endangered species of animals.

regions.name: Keibul Lamjao
features: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in the state of Manipur.
It is the only floating National park in the world.
It is a wetland ecosystem.

regions.name: Manas
features: Manas National Park is located in the state of Assam.
It was declared as a National Park in 1990.
It covers an area of 2837 Square Kilometres and has dense forests and grasslands.
It has the largest number of protected species in India.
